text: You're typing a quick message, but your phone keeps changing your words to something nonsensical.
You try to fix it, but the autocorrect insists it knows better, stubbornly offering the wrong word again.
You wonder, is it trying to be funny, or is it broken? You search for the 'why' behind these bizarre corrections.
The system isn't broken; it's learning. It analyzes millions of texts to find the most frequent 'typos' people make.
Your individual correction is ignored because the collective mistake is statistically more common across all users.
So, the 'wrong' autocorrect is actually the most common error, learned from countless others, not a personal attack on your typing.
